title: Assessment: Chemical Reactions in the Environment
description: Checkpoint assessment on environmental chemical reactions, local examples, reaction products, and common misconceptions.

questions.question: Which situation is the best example of combustion in the environment?
options: Rainwater slowly evaporating from a road
LPG burning in a kitchen stove
A magnet sticking to an iron gate
questions.explanation: LPG burning is combustion because fuel reacts with oxygen and releases heat and light. Evaporation and dissolving are physical changes.

questions.question: A student observes bubbles when dilute acid touches a strip of magnesium. Which product explains the bubbles?
questions.explanation: Acids reacting with many active metals produce a salt and hydrogen gas. The bubbles are evidence of the hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which product set is expected when acid reacts with calcium carbonate in limestone?
questions.explanation: Acid + carbonate reactions produce a salt, water, and carbon dioxide. This is why carbonate materials fizz with acid.

questions.question: True or False: Acid rain is usually weak, but repeated exposure can still damage stone and metal surfaces over time.
questions.explanation: True. Acid rain does not instantly destroy materials, but repeated wetting can slowly corrode metals and dissolve carbonate surfaces.

questions.question: Which pair of pollutants can help form acid rain after reacting in the atmosphere?
options: Water vapor and pure nitrogen only
questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels can react with oxygen and water in air to form acidic substances.

questions.question: Explain one way combustion is helpful and one way it can harm the environment.
questions.correctAnswer: Combustion is helpful because it releases energy for cooking, transportation, or electricity. It can harm the environment by releasing carbon dioxide and pollutants such as smoke, nitrogen oxides, or carbon monoxide when burning is incomplete.
questions.explanation: A complete answer should show the tradeoff: combustion supplies useful energy, but its products can affect climate and air quality.

questions.question: The general pattern for acid + metal is: acid + metal -> salt + ____ gas.
questions.explanation: Acids reacting with many metals produce a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: True or False: Bubbles always prove that water is boiling and never indicate a chemical reaction.
questions.explanation: False. Bubbles can come from boiling, but they can also show gas production in a chemical reaction, such as hydrogen or carbon dioxide forming.

questions.question: A marble marker near a busy road becomes dull and pitted after years of rain exposure. Which explanation best fits the lesson?
options: The marble changed only because sunlight melted it
Acidic rainwater reacted slowly with carbonate in the marble
The marble absorbed oxygen and became gasoline
The rain turned the marble into pure iron
questions.explanation: Marble contains calcium carbonate. Acidic rainwater can react with carbonate and gradually etch or pit the surface.

questions.question: A student says, 'Acid + metal and acid + carbonate both make the same gas because both fizz.' Correct the statement.
questions.correctAnswer: They can both fizz, but the gases are different. Acid + metal usually produces hydrogen gas, while acid + carbonate produces carbon dioxide gas.
questions.explanation: The same visible evidence, bubbles, can come from different gases. The reactants determine which gas forms.

questions.question: Which action would best reduce corrosion risk for an outdoor metal gate in a humid Philippine coastal community?
options: Remove all paint so rain can wash the metal directly
Keep it scratched to expose fresh metal
Apply and maintain a protective coating or paint
questions.explanation: Protective coatings limit contact between the metal and water, oxygen, salt, and acidic pollutants, reducing corrosion risk.

questions.question: In acid rain damage to limestone, the gas produced by the acid-carbonate reaction is ____.
questions.explanation: Limestone contains calcium carbonate. Acid + carbonate reactions produce a salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas.
